terms.definition: Amazon Machine Image — a template containing the OS, software, and configuration needed to launch an EC2 instance
terms.example: Like a cookie cutter — the AMI defines the shape, and EC2 instances are the cookies you bake from it

terms.definition: An AMI you create yourself from a running EC2 instance, capturing its exact software configuration for reuse
terms.example: You install Apache on an EC2 instance, create a custom AMI, and now every new instance launched from it already has Apache

terms.definition: AWS-provided AMIs containing clean operating system installations maintained and patched by AWS
terms.example: Amazon Linux 2023, Ubuntu 22.04, Windows Server 2022 — all available under Quick Start

terms.definition: AMIs published by third-party vendors on the AWS Marketplace, often with commercial software pre-installed
terms.example: A vendor might publish a pre-configured WordPress or database AMI with a licensing fee

terms.definition: Elastic Block Store volume — the virtual hard disk attached to a running EC2 instance where the OS and data live
terms.example: Like the physical hard drive inside a laptop — it holds everything while the machine is running

terms.definition: A point-in-time backup of an EBS volume that captures only the used data blocks
terms.example: An 8 GB EBS volume with 1.6 GB of actual data produces a 1.6 GB snapshot

terms.definition: The state an AMI enters immediately after creation, while AWS is still processing and registering it
terms.example: After clicking 'Create Image', the AMI shows 'pending' for a few minutes before becoming available

terms.definition: The state indicating an AMI is fully created and ready to be used to launch EC2 instances
terms.example: Once the AMI status shows 'available', you can select it under My AMIs when launching a new instance

terms.definition: The action to remove/delete an AMI template from your account — does NOT delete the underlying EBS snapshot
terms.example: Actions → Deregister AMI removes the template; you must separately delete the snapshot to free storage

terms.definition: The AWS action that duplicates an AMI from one region to another, creating a new independent copy with its own AMI ID
terms.example: Copying an AMI from Mumbai to North Virginia lets you launch identical servers in the US region

terms.definition: A standardized, organization-approved AMI containing a pre-hardened, pre-configured baseline used consistently across all environments
terms.example: A company creates a monthly golden AMI with the latest OS patches — all teams must launch servers from this

terms.definition: An AWS resource that exists only in the region where it was created and must be explicitly copied or recreated to be used elsewhere
terms.example: AMIs are region-specific — an AMI in Mumbai is not visible or usable when your console is set to North Virginia

terms.definition: The tab in the EC2 launch wizard that shows AMIs you have created yourself (custom AMIs)
terms.example: When launching an instance, click 'My AMIs' instead of 'Quick Start' to use your custom template

terms.definition: Hardware Virtual Machine — the virtualization type used by all modern EC2 instances, providing full hardware virtualization
terms.example: All current EC2 AMIs use HVM virtualization; the older PV (Paravirtual) type is legacy

terms.definition: Amazon's managed DNS service that translates domain names into IP addresses and routes traffic to AWS resources
terms.example: Map www.mywebsite.com to your EC2 instance's IP using Route 53 — covered in an upcoming session

terms.definition: An enterprise IT service management platform used for incident ticketing and routing support requests to the right departments
terms.example: A company uses ServiceNow to automatically route server outage tickets to the infrastructure team

terms.definition: An enterprise HR and people management platform used internally for performance tracking, leave management, and payroll
terms.example: Employees use Workday to request time off and check their pay stubs

terms.definition: An EC2 feature that lets you specify a mix of instance types and AWS automatically selects the cheapest available option
terms.example: Define T2, T3, and M5 as options — Spot Fleet picks whichever is cheapest at launch time

terms.definition: A mandatory statutory retirement benefit in India where both employer and employee contribute a percentage of salary
terms.example: A company with more than 20 employees in India is legally required to provide PF to all employees

terms.definition: The charge for storing EBS snapshots, billed per GB per month (approximately $0.05/GB in most regions)
terms.example: A 1.6 GB snapshot costs about $0.08/month — remember to delete unused snapshots to avoid charges
